In each independent case, a new partner brings a cash premium for goodwill, and the existing partners sacrifice part of their shares. Match each situation in List-I with its accounting treatment in List-II.

List-I
(A) The new partner pays the premium directly and privately to the existing partners.
(B) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to Premium for Goodwill A/c.
(C) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to the new partner’s capital account before distribution to the sacrificing partners.
(D) The premium has been credited to the existing partners’ capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio, and they retain the amount in the business.

List-II
(I) No entry is passed in the firm’s books.
(II) Bank A/c Dr. to Premium for Goodwill A/c; then Goodwill A/c Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(III) Bank A/c Dr. to the new partner’s capital account; then the new partner’s capital account Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(IV) No additional entry is passed for retaining the credited amounts in the business.
